messages:
maria: Heads up — since last week's canary we're seeing host-side CPU on the ingress proxy spike for lots of tiny streaming requests. p99 decode latency up ~18% and syscall rate is through the roof.

devon: Can you attach the flamegraph/pprof? Which processes are hot?

maria: Quick grab from prod-canal-7a (pprof): syscall rate dominated by writev/sys_write, then our parse_token and stream-chunker paths. Also epoll_wait churn. I'll paste a trimmed perf top.

zhang: ```
Samples:  1000K of event 'cpu-clock'
  18.3%  ingress-proxy  [.] writev
  12.7%  ingress-proxy  [.] parse_token
  10.5%  ingress-proxy  [.] stream_chunker::emit_frame
   9.8%  ingress-proxy  [.] kernel_selector::choose
   8.9%  libc-2.31     [.] sys_write
   6.2%  ingress-proxy  [.] kv_cache::lookup
```

maria: Interesting — I cross-checked with the rollout commits. Commit abc123 changed kernel_selector to prefer the new fp16 path for short sequences (saves token compute on GPU) but it adds a cpu-side fp32->fp16 conversion when requests are short and synchronous, which is hitting the host.

devon: That explains the kernel_selector line. But the writev/syscall domination suggests lots of tiny frames. Are we emitting many small chunks per request?

samir: Yes — streaming chunker currently flushes on every terminal token and on partial frames. For small prompts (<=32 tokens) we often send 3-6 tiny frames of ~300-800 bytes. On high QPS that multiplies syscalls.

maria: Proposed mitigations:
- coalesce outgoing frames in the proxy into an 8KB write buffer (coalesce until size or timeout)
- change batching heuristic to weight candidates by token_count instead of request_count (prefer to fill by tokens)
- KV cache: increase hot shard prefetch window and reduce LRU churn for sub-1s sessions

devon: microbench idea: compare syscall counts with and without writev coalescing. If we cut syscalls by ~3-4x we should see p99 latency drop. I'll craft a quick harness.

zhang: Quick draft patch for coalescing (concept):
```rust
// pseudo
let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
for frame in frames {
  if buf.len() + frame.len() > 8192 {
    socket.writev(&buf_chunks);
    buf.clear();
  }
  buf.extend_from_slice(&frame);
}
if !buf.is_empty() { socket.writev(&buf_chunks); }
```

samir: Ran a small experiment in staging: coalesce -> writev calls/sec down 3.2x, p99 down ~12%, mean down ~7% on tiny-chunk workload. No obvious regressions in throughput.

joni: What about gRPC/http2/hpack overhead? Are header churn and small HEADERS frames a problem too?

zhang: gRPC path adds HPACK work for frequent small headers (auth ephemeral tokens). Tracer shows many small HEADERS frames. We should: pin common headers in the connection's dynamic table where possible and avoid per-chunk auth header if we can use a short-lived session token on the channel.

devon: Also the kernel_selector change: for short sequences the cpu conversion overhead may nullify GPU savings. Can we make selector aware of end-to-end host latency (if host_cpu_percent > X, prefer fp32 kernel)?

maria: Good call. Let's implement a soft-fallback: if host-side cpu per-request estimate over window > 10ms, prefer kernels with less host work. Also add a metric: ingress_writev_calls/sec and ingress_avg_coalesced_bytes.

samir: Another quick config tweak that helped: change batching heuristic to token-weighted with a cap on max_wait_ms=12 for low-latency tier. Reduced mis-batching where many tiny requests blocked larger helpful joins.

devon: I'll push canary of: coalesce writev + token-weighted batch heuristic + kernel_selector fallback to infra canary lane (canary-3) at 10:05 UTC. infra-bot will post deploy status.

infra-bot: deploy_bot: started canary canary-3 for ingress-proxy @ 10:05 UTC; sha=def456. Rolling 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% if no errors.

maria: After canary, capture pprof and writev metrics. If p99 improvement holds and error budget okay, roll. Also create a follow-up task: add unit tests for coalescing logic and an e2e latency test with tiny-chunk workload. :thumbsup:

joni: Also note to docs: update runtime tuning guide to mention token-weighted batching and when to prefer coalescing.

devon: Will follow up with a short RFC for the kernel_selector policy change (cost-aware selection).
